title: This grand Welsh castle is said to be haunted, and you can stay the night
excerpt: This prestigious wedding venue is also one of the most haunted castles in Wales

The spooky season is almost here, and many paranormal fans will be wondering where the best ghost-hunting spots in Wales are. Ever witnessed something that gave you chills or heard a strange noise in the dead of night and dismissed it as your imagination? If you're brave enough to face the unknown, why not test your nerve by spending the night in one of Wales' haunted hotels, castles, or inns?

These chilling places have it all: history, grandiose design, and countless reports of unsettling encounters over the years with phantom footsteps, ghostly figures, and eerie whispers in the dark. Yikes

It’s no surprise that paranormal investigators from far and wide flock here, hoping to catch a glimpse of the ghosts said to roam these historic sites.

One place in particular is worth spending the night if you love a spine-tingling stay is - Craig y Nos Castle. This prestigious wedding venue is also one of the most haunted castles in Wales, offering accommodation for wedding guests and ghost hunters who want a spooky bed-and-breakfast stay.

The Castle and Country Park sits alongside the upper River Tawe on the edge of the Black Mountains, with several local walks starting directly from your room.

It's open to the public year-round, and admission is free. The castle has two car parks with free parking for visitors and guests.

According to Haunted Rooms, Craig y Nos Castle was originally built in 1843 by Captain Rice Powell. However, in 1898, the famous opera singer Adelina Patti fell in love with the castle and made it her home.

Patti gained worldwide fame due to the exceptional quality of her voice and her ability to perform "vocal gymnastics" effortlessly.

Between tours, she recharged and entertained her many friends at Craig-y-Nos Castle on Brecon Road, according to the venue's website.

Patti transformed the property into a luxurious retreat, hosting elite guests such as Henry of Battenberg, the Crown Prince of Sweden, and even Edward VII.

After Patti’s death, the castle took a much darker turn and was converted into a tuberculosis hospital and later a care home for the elderly.

The castle didn’t return to private ownership until 1986. With so many lives lost within its walls, it's no surprise the castle is said to be haunted.

The most notorious location is what used to be the children’s ward – now considered the most paranormally active room.

Visitors have reported hearing children's laughter, seeing ghostly figures, and even hearing the eerie sound of bouncing balls in the dead of night.

Patti is also rumoured to haunt the castle. She was embalmed in the castle's cellar. People have reported experiencing high-pitched noises and the sensation of objects, such as tables and chairs, moving.

Today, haunting stays and chilling ghost tours are on offer, with members guided through the venue's most haunted rooms.

These include the theatre basement, where Adelina Patti once made her stage debut; the children's ward at the end of a long, dark corridor, complete with original light fittings; and the treatment room, once home to tuberculosis patients in the 1920s.

Perhaps one of the most unnerving elements of the tour is the room of John Mellon, who was said to be an employee of Adelina Patti and suffered an untimely death in a room on the building's top floor.

During an episode of Most Haunted, psychic Derek Acorah said he felt as though he was being pushed out of its window.

For those brave enough, there is also an opportunity to stay as a guest on a short B&B break, a dog-friendly getaway or a budget-friendly family holiday.

According to its website, the castle has 36 rooms in total with a bar, kitchen, gym and dining facilities "for the perfect break away".

Most rooms at Craig-y-Nos are en-suite doubles, family rooms or apartments, with two rooms equipped with disabled facilities.

A separate block of budget rooms without en-suite facilities is available, comprising nine doubles and one single room. Many rooms feature fine period details, classic florals, and oak.

You can also enjoy dinner in the main dining room, or you can dine and unwind in the dog-friendly Patti Bar.

Craig-y-Nos also offers several Ghost Tour packages for couples, friends, or individuals looking to join other enthusiastic ghost hunters.
